{{short description|Ukrainian mathematician}}
'''Svitlana Mayboroda''' ({{Langx|uk|Світлана Майборода}}; born 1981) is a Ukrainian mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Minnesota]]<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://math.umn.edu/~svitlana/Vitae.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Svitlana Mayboroda|access-date=2015-11-18}}.</ref> and [[ETH Zurich]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-08-04 |title=Svitlana Mayboroda newly appointed professor |url=https://math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news/d-math-news/2023/08/svitlana-mayboroda-newly-appointed-professor.html |access-date=2023-08-11 |website=math.ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref> and is a Distinguished Visiting Professor at the [https://www.ias.edu/ Institute for Advanced Study].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute for Advanced Study |date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/svitlana-mayboroda}}</ref>

==Research==
Mayboroda's research concerns [[harmonic analysis]] geometric measure theory and [[partial differential equation]]s, including [[boundary value problem]]s for [[elliptic partial differential equation]]s.<ref name="sadosky"/> In particular, her work has provided a new mathematical approach to [[Anderson localization]], a phenomenon in physics in which waves are confined to a local region rather than propagating throughout a medium, and has enjoyed wide ranging applications in condensed matter physics, cold atoms systems, research and engineering of organic and nonorganic semiconductor materials and devices.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematician-tames-rogue-waves-illuminating-future-of-led-lighting-20170822/|magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]|title=Mathematician Tames Rogue Waves, Illuminating Future of LED Lighting|first=Kevin|last=Hartnett|date=August 22, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=TerryTao: Svitlana Mayboroda Tag |url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/tag/svitlana-mayboroda/ |access-date=2025-10-16}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Mayboroda was born on June 2, 1981, in [[Kharkiv]]. She earned the Ukrainian equivalent of two master's degrees, one in finance and one in applied mathematics, from the [[University of Kharkiv]] in 2001, and completed her Ph.D. in 2005 from the [[University of Missouri]] under the supervision of Marius Mitrea.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=41018}}</ref> After visiting positions at the [[Australian National University]], [[Ohio State University]], and [[Brown University]], she joined the [[Purdue University]] faculty in 2008, and moved to the University of Minnesota in 2011.<ref name="cv"/> In 2023, she joined the ETH Zurich faculty.<ref name=":0" />

==Recognition==
Mayboroda was a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]] for 2010–2015.<ref name="cv"/>
In 2013, she became the inaugural winner of the [[Sadosky Prize|Sadosky Research Prize in Analysis]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name="sadosky">{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-sadosky-research-prize/awm-sadosky-research-prize-2014/|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=2015-11-18|title=AWM-Sadosky Research Prize in Analysis}}.</ref>
In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2015-11-18}}.</ref> In 2016, she was awarded the first Northrop Professorship at the University of Minnesota.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www2.math.umn.edu/news/2016/4/6/svitlana-mayboroda-awarded-first-northrop-professorship-u-m/ |title=News - math.umn.edu |website=www2.math.umn.edu |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160421211604/http://www2.math.umn.edu/news/2016/4/6/svitlana-mayboroda-awarded-first-northrop-professorship-u-m/ |archive-date=21 April 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 2020 she became the McKnight Presidential Professor.<ref name="McKnight">{{citation|url=https://cse.umn.edu/math/news/professor-svitlana-mayboroda-awarded-mcknight-presidential-professorship|publisher=[[University of Minnesota]]|access-date=2024-09-25|title=McKnight Presidential Professorship}}.</ref> She was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking in the section on Analysis and Operator Algebras.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-speakers|title=Speakers|work=ICM 2018|access-date=2018-02-24|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215001530/http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-speakers|archive-date=2017-12-15}}</ref> She became the 2023 National Blavatnik Laureate in Physical Sciences & Engineering, given to an outstanding scientist under the age of 42.<ref>url= http://blavatnikawards.org/news/items/2023-blavatnik-national-awards-young-scientists-announced/</ref> That same year, she was also elected to the European Academy of Sciences,<ref name="Academy">{{citation|url=https://math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news/d-math-news/2024/09/svitlana-mayboroda-elected-to-european-academy-of-sciences.html|publisher=[[ETH Zurich]]|access-date=2024-09-25|title=European Academy of Sciences|date=6 September 2024 }}.</ref> and, together with Marcel Filoche, was awarded the Elias M. Stein Prize for New Perspectives in Analysis<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-14 |title=News from the AMS. Filoche and Mayboroda Awarded Inaugural 2024 Elias M. Stein Prize for New Perspectives in Analysis |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7250 |access-date=2026-01-05 |website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> by the [https://www.ams.org/home/page American Mathematical Society, AMS]. In 2025, Mayboroda was elected to the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]  for her contributions to mathematical analysis and partial differential equations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leopoldina |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/svitlana-mayboroda/ |access-date=2025-10-16}}</ref>  She is also an elected member of the [[Academia Europaea]], recognizing her distinguished scholarship in mathematics .<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Svitlana Mayboroda |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Mayboroda_Svitlana |access-date=2025-10-16}}</ref> In the same year, she received the [https://math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news/d-math-news/2025/07/svitlana-mayboroda-honoured-with-blaise-pascal-medal.html Blaise Pascal Medal in Mathematics] from the [https://www.eurasc.eu/ European Academy of Sciences (EurASc)], awarded for outstanding contributions to the theory of elliptic partial differential equations and spectral theory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blaise Pascal Medal in Mathematics |date=16 July 2025 |url=https://math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news/d-math-news/2025/07/svitlana-mayboroda-honoured-with-blaise-pascal-medal.html |access-date=2025-10-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite |website=2025-10-16}}</ref><ref name="Simons">{{citation |title=Simons Collaboration on Localization of Waves |url=https://cse.umn.edu/wave |access-date=2024-09-25 |publisher=[[University of
